title: Agreed: an immediate motion of the will, not an abiding habit
source_text: XLVII. Constat quidem inter utrosque gratiam illam, sine qua nullus ad Deum convertitur & bene agit, & quam omnes qui accipiunt, certo & infallibiliter convertuntur & bene agunt, esse auxilium quoddam quod voluntatem ipsam per se & immediate movet atque afficit, non vero intellectum solum; nec eam in ullo habitu permanenti constituendam esse. Sed quid illa sit, inter hos & illos non omnino convenit: imo nequidem inter ipsos Thomistas.
pass_a_gloss: XLVII. It is agreed indeed between both that that grace, without which no one is converted to God and acts well, and which all who receive, certainly and infallibly are converted and act well, is a certain help which moves and affects the will itself by itself and immediately, not however the intellect alone; nor is it to be placed in any permanent habit. But what it is, is not altogether agreed between these and those: nay not even among the Thomists themselves.
pass_b_english: Thesis XLVII. Both sides agree that the grace without which no one turns to God and does good, and whose recipients are all surely and infallibly converted and do good, is an aid that moves and affects the will itself, of itself and immediately, and not the intellect alone; and that it is not to be located in any abiding habit.
But what it is, the two sides do not fully agree; indeed, not even the Thomists agree among themselves.
